data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The result is a tautology of the registry convention: the registry records what the tests say, not what the guards do, so under shown-to-fail-first installation the recorded distribution is a description of the test's own reach by construction, and any 'constraint' is only the registry's restatement of the test's failure channel.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If at least one registry entry were written by a guard firing without a prior test failure, the by-construction claim would break.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the registry distinguished test-caught from guard-caught, the tautology would be resolved into a description.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If a mutation could be recorded as lost even when the test passed and the guard fired, the registry would not merely restate the test.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Because the installation ritual is shown-to-fail-first, the registry's entry for a mutation is written by the test's failure, not by the guard's verdict. The 3-of-26 count and the 1/9 compile.py loss are then restatements of which mutations the test channel can touch, and the 4/4 to 6/7 banding is the registry's serialisation of that channel. Nothing independent of the test is measured.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
